newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes mixed, Oman trades below MPM plus 10.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes mixed, Oman trades below MPM plus 10.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia were mixed on Wednesday with most wet trade once against focused on the Oman market.
A U.S. major was confirmed taking three cargoes of Oman crude at MPM plus 8.5 cents to plus nine cents. The sellers were two Japanese traders and another U.S. major.
One of the Japanese traders had bought Oman at MPM plus eight cents and earlier this week at plus 10 cents, representing the strongest Oman premium for December barrels to date.
Traders said a European major sold 200,000 barrels of Oman crude at MPM plus nine cents to a Japanese refinery.
Two Qatar Lands were said done, one to a U.S. major at a premium of around 39 cents to QGPC and another to a separate U.S. major at plus 32 cents.
One of the remaining Murban cargos for December was sold at a premium of ADNOC plus 60 cents, traders said. The cargo went to a U.S. major from a Japanese trader, market sources said.

A December cargo of 650,000 barrels of North West Shelf condensate was sold by an operator at Arun quotes plus 71 cents, surpassing the value of the last November North West Shelf condensate, which was sold for Arun plus 60/65 cents by a European major.
A rival seller of North West Shelf was offering a late December cargo at Arun plus $1.00.
Traders said there was market talk that China had aquired 1.6 million barrels of Alaskan North Slope crude. Traders said the price was based on Arab Light quotes or even Oman MPM basis.
Traders said they were looking to the Bangchak tender for December crude, which closes later on Wednesday, for further indications on the outlook for Oman's December market.
The tender is expected to be awarded on Thursday, although the November tender was not immediately awarded on the validity date, traders said.
